newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet continues plans to buy new MD-95 jets.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet continues plans to buy new MD-95 jets.

text.p: ValuJet Inc Chairman Lewis Jordan said Tuesday his carrier planned to go ahead with its purchase of new McDonnell Douglas Corp MD-95 jet aircraft.

The low-cost, Atlanta-based airline agreed last year to buy 50 of the new 100-seat jets with an option to buy 50 additional ones. But the planned purchase seemed to be in jeopardy following the grounding of the carrier last June 17.
But Jordan said in a speech today, "We do plan to operate these airplanes."
Jordan said he had met with McDonnell Douglas officials last Friday to review details of the new plane, for which ValuJet will be the launch purchaser.
"We think it is a terrific airplane," Jordan told a meeting of the Global Aviation and Security Summit.
Jordan declined to discuss the causes of the crash of ValuJet flight 592 into the Everglades in Florida last May 11, which killed all 110 people aboard.

No cause of the accident has yet been officially determined, but National Transportation Safety Board investigators believe it may have been due to a fire that started in oxygen canisters being carried in the plane's cargo hold.

Five weeks after the crash, following an intensive review of its operations by the Federal Aviation Administration, the airline was grounded, and it remained grounded until it was allowed to resume limited operations on September 26.

Jordan said ValuJet has since hired new staff and reinforced emphasis on safety, adding that all airlines should put less stress on what has happened in the past and be more forward-looking to try to prevent future accidents.
He said his airline would be happy to work with others to contribute to a pool of information to improve airline safety.
"ValuJet volunteers to play a role. We're dedicated to that proposition," Jordan said.
Asked what lessons could be learned from the crash, he said, "Safety can never be over-emphasized."
